outcome: Admission to neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: Singleton pregnancies at risk for macrosomia without contraindication to vaginal delivery, receiving an ultrasound scan at 34-37 weeks of pregnancy
finding: A false-positive diagnosis of LGA is associated with a significant increase in cesarean sections during labor, suggesting that a suspicious ultrasound may lead to a lower clinical threshold for diagnosing abnormal labor.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rate during labor was significantly higher in FP LGA than in AGA (19% vs. 8.7%) but not significantly different between FP LGA and TP LGA (19% vs. 32.4%).
